newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-ENGLISH PENPIX FOR TOURNOI DE FRANCE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ENGLISH PENPIX FOR TOURNOI DE FRANCE.

text.p: Profiles of the England squad for the Tournoi de France starting on Tuesday:
Goalkeepers:

David Seaman (Arsenal) age 33, 34 caps. Joined Arsenal for 1.3 million pounds sterling ($2.1 million) from Queens Park Rangers in 1990 which was then a record fee for an English goalkeeper. Had an outstanding Euro'96 and now back in action after missing matches against Italy and Mexico through injury.

Tim Flowers (Blackburn Rovers) 30, 8. Currently Seaman's understudy in the international squad although he has not played a full international since England met China a year ago. Moved from Southampton to Blackburn for 2.4 million pounds ($3.8 million) in 1993, still the record for an English 'keeper.

Nigel Martyn (Leeds United) 30, 4. Made his first England appearance for four years when he played against South Africa on May 24. Had a superb season at Leeds but was at fault for South Africa's goal in England's 2-1 win.
Defenders:

Gary Neville (Manchester United) 22, 19. Two years older than brother Philip, a fellow squad member. Against China a year ago, they became the first brothers to play together for England for 26 years. Excellent tackler, fast and has just enjoyed an excellent season with Manchester United.

Gareth Southgate (Aston Villa) 26, 16. Influential captain and midfielder for Crystal Palace before moving to Aston Villa in 1994. Now plays in the backline. His failure to score in the semifinal shootout against Germany saw England eliminated from Euro'96. Played well against Poland on Saturday with several timely defensive interceptions.

Martin Keown (Arsenal) 30, 13. Recalled to the England side against Mexico in March for the first time in four years. With his club-mate Tony Adams and Gary Pallister missing the tournament through injury, he has the chance to add to his total of caps.

Sol Campbell (Tottenham) 22, 7. Solid, reliable and a tower of strength in defence, although his distribution sometimes lets him down. Among the youngsters in the squad, looks set for a great future and had his best match for England against Poland on Saturday.

Stuart Pearce (Nottingham Forest) 35, 75. Took over as Forest player-manager at Christmas but could not save them from relegation. Has since reverted to player status only and has two burning ambitions for next year -- to see Forest promoted and play for England in the World Cup finals.

Graeme Le Saux (Blackburn Rovers) 28, 17 caps. Has recovered from a possible career-ending ankle injury and played in England's last five internationals. Became the first player from the Channel Islands to win a full England cap when he made his debut against Denmark in 1994. Determined, insdustrious and a good crosser of the ball.

Philip Neville (Manchester United) 20, 3 caps. The youngest player in the squad, he won his second cap against South Africa at his home ground of Old Trafford last week. Like brother Gary a regular in the Manchester United side and before too long will probably be a regular for England as well.
Midfielders:

Paul Ince (Inter Milan) 29, 30. Has captained England in the past and is vital to the team's midfield. Hard-tackling when defending, creative when attacking as he proved in Poland, providing a great long pass which led to the opening goal. Moved from Manchester United to Inter Milan a year ago and despite talk of a transfer looks set to stay in Italy.

Lee Clark (Sunderland), 24, 0. His late call-up into the squad in place of Manchester United's injured Nicky Butt coincided with his close-season transfer from Newcastle United to neighbours Sunderland. Hard-working midfielder who found it hard to win a regular place at Newcastle.

Paul Gascoigne (Glasgow Rangers) 30, 48. Turned 30 last week, with his career again at the crossroads and his turbulent personal life again under the media microscope. On his day a brilliant player who can win a match, on an off-day can be a huge liability. Injured against Poland and now doubtful for the Tournoi.

David Beckham (Manchester United) 22, 7 caps. Made his England debut against Moldova last September, two weeks after scoring from the halfway line against Wimbledon. Lost form towards the end of the season but nevertheless an outstanding talent with great movement and vision. English newspaper reports say he is about to get married to Spice Girl Victoria Adams.

Robert Lee (Newcastle United) 31, 11. Scored the opening goal against South Africa, his first goal for England since a debut strike in 1994. Played more than 300 matches for Charlton before moving to Newcastle in 1992. Strong versatile midfielder.

David Batty (Newcastle United) 28, 24. Terrier-like midfielder who battles hard for every ball. Once had an on-field altercation with fellow squad member Le Saux when they were both at Blackburn. Coach Glenn Hoddle revived his England career after injury forced him out of contention for last year's European Championship.
Strikers:

Alan Shearer (Newcastle United) 26, 33 caps. The England captain set a world transfer record of 15 million pounds ($24 million) when he moved from Blackburn to Newcastle last July. Top scorer in Euro'96 with five goals he has also scored five in six World Cup matches this season and 10 in his last 10 internationals. Superb striker at the peak of his career.

Teddy Sheringham (Tottenham Hotspur) 31, 25. Has scored four goals in his last five internationals. Relatively slow for a striker but makes up for it by his speed of thought. Has formed an excellent understanding with Shearer in attack.

Paul Scholes (Manchester United) 22, 1. Made his debut as a substitute at Old Trafford against South Africa last week. Dangerous in front of goal with the in-built knack of all great scorers, being in the right place at the right time.

Ian Wright (Arsenal) 33, 34. Revealed at the end of May he has been to counselling to try and curb a hot temper which has caused him many on-field problems. Should become Arsenal's all-time record scorer next season. A superb, intuitive player with a catalogue of great goals to his credit. Scored his sixth England goal against South Africa.

Andy Cole (Manchester United) 25, 1. Has had two disappointing years at Old Trafford since his move from Newcastle in 1995 but ended the season showing glimpses of his old scoring form and recalled to the squad as a late replacement for the injured Les Ferdinand.
